key_insight: Agentic RSR unifies scene reconstruction, policy learning, and real-robot execution in one real-to-sim-to-real loop, so the simulated environment stays grounded in what the robot can actually see and do. The core idea is to reconstruct a task-relevant workspace from video and use that same task to train and validate robot policies.
problem_solved: Traditional real-to-sim workflows often separate scene reconstruction from policy design, which can create a mismatch between simulated scenes and real robot observations. This paper addresses the challenge of building simulations that preserve task-relevant interactions while training policies that remain executable on the real robot.
method: Use a workspace video, task description, and known robot model as inputs to reconstruct the scene in simulation.
Link scene reconstruction and policy development through the same manipulation task, instead of treating them as separate steps.
Ground policy learning in observations and execution constraints available to the real robot, then transfer the resulting policy back to physical execution.
impact: This matters because it reduces the sim-to-real gap in manipulation tasks by making the simulator more faithful to real robot perception and interaction. For practitioners, it offers a more practical pipeline for building deployable policies with less manual scene engineering and fewer transfer failures.

paper_title: Agentic RSR: Real-to-Sim-to-Real through Scene Reconstruction and Execution-Grounded Robot Policies
paper_authors: Yihan Li, Yating Feng, Shengjiu Sun, Jianing Chen, Hao Ren
